text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
Brazilian workers will be able to use up to 50 percent of the money they are entitled to under a special fund for buying into state firms being privatized.
Constran International Ltd, a Cayman Islands subsidiary of Brazil's Constran S.A. Construcoes e Comercio, failed to make a $13 million payment on its euro-commercial paper program on Tuesday.
--JUDGE TO TRY 16 PARENTS FOR LETTING KIDS BEG
A Rio judge says he will try 16 parents for forcing their kids to beg in the street.
-- CONDE MOVES UP AND SERGIO FALLS IN POLLS
Rio mayoral candidate Luiz Paulo Conde moved up three points to 50 percent in the latest poll and his rival Sergio Cabral Filho fell three points to 26 percent.
-- GOVERNMENT WANTS SCHOOLS TO RESOLVE DEBT
The government is considering requiring schools to renegotiate debt owed to them by parents who can't pay their bills.
Murder, suicides and traffic accidents is responsible for 70 percent of the deaths of Brazilian men between the ages of 15 and 29.
* Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
